description: Hand-maintained inputs for tools/generate_validation_matrix.py. Everything a runner already declares (which placements and quantization formats it supports) is read from its LoadDeclaration and must not be repeated here. This file holds only what cannot be derived: what each hardware profile can attempt, how many ranks a placement gets, and which models need an input this harness cannot supply.
world_size_rationale: One rank for eager because it shards nothing. The multi-rank default is deliberately conservative for profiles whose machines are small; a profile whose hardware ships more devices should override it, because testing a rank count nobody deploys measures a configuration that does not exist. Profiles override this with their own world_size_policy.

profiles.world_size_note: Eight ranks because an MI300X or MI355X node ships eight devices and that is how these models are actually served, so a four-rank result would describe a deployment nobody runs.
profiles.runtime_args_note: Taken from .ci/benchmark_configs, where every eight-GPU Instinct entry pins attention_backend: aiter and use_torch_compile: true. Both were previously left unset: attention selection happened to resolve to AITER anyway, so the sweep agreed with production by accident and would have drifted silently if the selector changed, while compile was simply never exercised even though nothing is served without it.

screening_plan.rationale: A screening set, not a full cross. Crossing placement by transformer quantization by text-encoder quantization is twelve cases per model, and running it for every model spends most of its time re-confirming that the same loading machinery works. These four cover every level of every factor, deliberately loading two of them densely: if a dense case fails, the model is expanded into the unconfounded cross to localize it. The bf16 sharded case is kept unconfounded on purpose, so a failure in the dense sharded case can be attributed by comparing the two rather than by re-running.

cases.role: reference for the image comparison, and the cheapest proof the model loads at all
the blockwise disk fill on its own, with nothing quantized to confuse a failure
dense: blockwise fill, per-block quantize and a quantized text encoder together
dense: broadcast fill with both quantizations, the path that has no per-block fill

quantizations_withheld.int8: TorchAO INT8 has no ROCm kernel path, so every case would be a rejection. Rejections stay curated: their value is a human asserting an external fact, which a generator reading the same probe code cannot do.
quantizations_withheld.fp4: The outcome differs across the two archs this token covers, since AITER ships no FP4 kernels for gfx942 but does for gfx950, so an FP4 case cannot share the pair token. The gfx950 FP4 cases are curated and pinned.
quantizations_withheld.fp8_fp4: Needs the FP4 half, so it inherits the same split.

requires_input_image.reason: These runners need a real input image or video, which the harness has no generic way to supply, so a generated case would fail for reasons unrelated to loading. Cases for them stay curated and pass the input through a placeholder.
